title: Anchor workload suite for kernel-selection & prefill/decode regression guards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an 'anchor' workload suite and CI guard framework that surfaces regressions related to kernel selection, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling. The suite should exercise corner-case kernel routing decisions (heterogeneous kernels, quantized vs float), attention kernel fastpaths (local vs flash attention), and realistic prefill/ decode mixes including KV cache hit/miss patterns. Outputs must be deterministic enough to be used as a CI perf gate while still covering stochastic workload variations seen in prod traces.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible anchor suite with at least 12 workload scenarios covering kernel routing edge cases, attention fastpath toggles, and prefill/decode mixes
Automated CI job that runs a lightweight microbench on every PR and triggers a full anchor-run on a weekly night schedule
Perf gates defined (P50, P95, token/sec) with documented thresholds and rollback/notify policy
Artifacts: canonical inputs, seed lists, and a golden results manifest stored in CI artifacts and an S3 bucket
Runbook describing when to widen thresholds, mark flaky scenarios, and launch triage playbooks
approach_steps: Survey existing workload corpus and identify 3 kernel-routing blindspots (short-decoder-heavy, long-prefill-heavy, hetero-layer-dtype mixes)
Implement deterministic workload synthesizer that replays sampled prod traces with fixed RNG seeds and time-of-day noise knobs
Add microbench harness modules: kernel_selector_probe, attention_fastpath_probe, prefill_decode_mixer
Instrument per-run telemetry to capture kernel decisions, chosen kernels per layer, KV cache hit ratio, and per-token latency buckets
Integrate lightweight PR-time job (5–10 min) vs nightly full anchor-run (60–90 min) with automatic artifact publishing
Define CI gate logic: PR-time warns on regressions >7% and blocks on weekly-run regressions >12% or sustained trend over 3 runs
tradeoffs: Longer CI runs increase CI cost and runner contention — mitigated by a tiered approach (fast microbench for PRs, heavier weekly runs)
Deterministic seeding reduces noise but can under-represent rare nondeterministic spikes; plan to include a small stochastic bucket for fuzz runs
Adding detailed telemetry increases disk/ingest costs — we will sample runs and compress kernel decision traces to conserve space

decision_log: Adopt two-tier CI: fast microbench on PRs (warn) + weekly full anchor-run (block on significant regressions)
Use deterministic seeds for primary golden runs and keep a separate stochastic fuzz bucket for rare events
Record kernel decision trace (layer->kernel mapping) for the top 10 slowest requests in each run to aid triage
risks: CI flakiness causing false positives if thresholds are too tight
Insufficient coverage of real-world request mixes may miss model-specific regressions
Cost of nightly full-runs may require infra quota adjustments or batching across teams
qa_steps: Run microbench locally with --seed=42 and verify produced P50/P95 matches golden manifest
Execute full nightly anchor-run on canary infra and compare kernel decision heatmaps to last 3 golden runs
Intentionally flip an attention fastpath flag and confirm CI warns/blocks per thresholds
Validate artifact upload to S3 and dashboard ingestion within 15 minutes of job completion
